## Purpose

The base-case model in this study prices every strategy using CMS Medicare-allowed
amounts, since that figure is uniform and publicly auditable nationwide. Medicaid and
commercial payer rates are not published by CMS and vary by hospital; the only public
source for them is the hospital-specific machine-readable file (MRF) every U.S. hospital
must publish under the CMS Hospital Price Transparency Rule (45 CFR 180). This supplement
documents two real-hospital MRF samples used for standalone sensitivity and validation
exercises in this study. **Neither sample is an input to the base-case cost-minimization
model**; both are reported here for transparency and as supporting evidence that the
base case's Medicare-anchored pricing is a reasonable approximation of real-world rates.

## Sample 1: six-hospital opportunity-cost sample

A convenience sample of six hospitals' MRFs, used to bound the commercial-margin-based
opportunity cost of displacing a colonoscopy-suite slot for a combined endometrial biopsy
add-on (`data/colonoscopy_multi_hospital_rates.csv`).

| Hospital | State |
|---|---|
| Denver Health Medical Center | CO |
| UCHealth University of Colorado Hospital | CO |
| Emory University Hospital | GA |
| University of Mississippi Medical Center | MS |

| NYU Langone Hospitals (Tisch) | NY |

## Sample 2: 74-hospital gynecologic oncology fellowship sample

A criterion-based sample -- all 75 ACGME-accredited gynecologic oncology fellowship
programs listed in AMA's FREIDA directory (one duplicate excluded, leaving 74 hospitals
attempted), tied directly to this study's clinical population rather than an arbitrary
convenience sample. Target codes: endometrial biopsy (CPT 58100), surgical pathology
(CPT 88305), dilation and curettage (CPT 58120), an established-patient office visit (CPT
99213), and colonoscopy. Of the 74 hospitals attempted, 41 returned usable data for every
target code, 26 returned usable data for some codes, and 7 returned none, each for a
documented reason.

## Cross-validation between the two samples

UCHealth University of Colorado Hospital appears in both samples, pulled independently on
different dates. The two independently-extracted Medicare rates for colonoscopy (HCPCS
G0105) matched exactly ($916.25), supporting the reliability of the extraction method
used for both samples.

## Known data-quality considerations

Several hospitals' files label a Medicaid managed-care plan's ACA-exchange product
generically as "Commercial"; duplicate chargemaster lines mapping the same procedure code
to different gross charges and negotiated rates are common enough that no single
hospital-level "commercial rate" exists for some codes without selecting a specific line;
and files exceeding approximately 1-2 GB could only be partially scanned, so a "no usable
data" result for a very large file is weaker evidence than the same result for a small
one.
